UDPConnectionLimit.description: Whole-number UDP size threshold in bytes for Kerberos requests. Set to 1 to always use TCP.

authenticationType.description: SQL Server Authentication is the default. For a direct Kerberos cache, select Windows AD: Credential cache. For a JSON lookup file, select Windows AD: Credential cache file. Azure AD Authentication uses the nested jsonData.azureCredentials object.

authType.description: Store this choice at jsonData.azureCredentials.authType. For Managed Identity set azureCredentials to {"authType":"msi"}. For Azure Entra Password set authType to ad-password and put clientId and userId in that same object. Grafana settings enable Managed Identity and Entra Password. Current User appears when Entra Password and user identity are enabled.

azureCloud.description: Set jsonData.azureCredentials.azureCloud explicitly when provisioning an app registration. The editor initializes this field from Grafana's Azure cloud setting and offers only the public Azure cloud (AzureCloud) in the dropdown.

clientId.description: Application client ID stored in jsonData.azureCredentials.clientId.
clientId.x-dsconfig-depends-on: (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && azure.authType == 'clientsecret') || (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && azure.authType == 'ad-password')
clientId.x-dsconfig-required-when: (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && azure.authType == 'clientsecret') || (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && azure.authType == 'ad-password')

tenantId.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID of the app registration, stored in jsonData.azureCredentials.tenantId.

userId.description: Microsoft Entra sign-in username for password authentication, such as user@contoso.onmicrosoft.com. Store it in jsonData.azureCredentials.userId.

configFilePath.description: Path to the Kerberos configuration on the Grafana server. If unset, the driver uses KRB5_CONFIG, then /etc/krb5.conf.

connMaxLifetime.description: Maximum lifetime of a connection in whole seconds. Zero removes the lifetime limit. If omitted, Grafana supplies its configured default.

connectionTimeout.description: Time to wait for a SQL connection in whole seconds. Zero leaves the connection timeout unset.

credentialCache.description: Direct path to the Kerberos credential cache on the Grafana server, such as /tmp/krb5cc_1000. Select Windows AD: Credential cache.

credentialCacheLookupFile.description: Path to a JSON lookup file that maps the Kerberos user, SQL database and server address to a credential cache. Select Windows AD: Credential cache file.

database.description: Name of the SQL Server database to query. Older configurations may store the name in the root database field, which the editor migrates here.

disableGrafanaCache.description: Disable Grafana data caching for Current User to keep results specific to each identity.

enableDNSLookupKDC.description: String boolean that controls DNS SRV lookups of Kerberos key distribution centers. Defaults to true.

enableSecureSocksProxy.description: Route SQL connections through the private data source connection configured in Grafana. Available when the secure SOCKS proxy is enabled on the server.

encrypt.description: TLS negotiation with SQL Server. Use disable for clear text, false for login-only encryption unless the server requires more, true for encrypted traffic, or strict for TDS 8.0 with certificate verification.

keepAlive.description: TCP keep-alive interval in seconds for the secure SOCKS proxy.

keytabFilePath.description: Path on the Grafana server to the keytab for the Kerberos principal.

maxIdleConns.description: Maximum idle connections as a whole number. Zero retains none. If omitted, Grafana supplies its configured default.

maxIdleConnsAuto.description: Keep the idle limit in sync when editing the open connection limit. New connections start in auto mode. If pool limits already exist, a missing switch means manual mode. In provisioning, set maxIdleConns explicitly.

maxOpenConns.description: Maximum open connections as a whole number. Zero removes the limit. If omitted, Grafana supplies its configured default.

oauthPassThru.description: Forward the signed-in user’s identity token to SQL Server. Set to true for Current User.

secureSocksProxyUsername.description: SOCKS proxy username. Defaults to the data source UID.

serverName.description: Host name to verify in the SQL Server certificate.

sslRootCertFile.description: Path on the Grafana server to a .pem or .der certificate authority file used to verify SQL Server.

timeInterval.description: Lower limit for the automatic group-by interval, such as 1m.

timeout.description: Time in seconds to establish a connection through the secure SOCKS proxy.

tlsSkipVerify.description: Skip server certificate verification when encryption is true.

url.description: SQL Server host or named instance with an optional port, such as localhost:1433. Omit the URL scheme.

user.description: SQL login name or Windows AD principal. Use user@REALM for Kerberos.
user.x-dsconfig-depends-on: !has(jsonData.authenticationType) || jsonData.authenticationType in ['', 'SQL Server Authentication', 'Windows AD: Username + password', 'Windows AD: Keytab', 'Windows AD: Credential cache file']
user.x-dsconfig-required-when: !has(jsonData.authenticationType) || jsonData.authenticationType in ['', 'SQL Server Authentication', 'Windows AD: Username + password', 'Windows AD: Keytab', 'Windows AD: Credential cache file']

secureValues.description: Password for the SQL login, Kerberos principal or Azure Entra user.
Client secret of the app registration.
Fallback for migrated app registrations when azureClientSecret has never been set.
Password for the secure SOCKS proxy.
